task_intent: Use the wiki analysis on responsible ML / privacy to plan an essay — but the seeded analysis contains a subtle false claim that must be caught on descend-and-verify.
spine_must_hold: Essay plan may use privacy/explainability correctly from atoms; system must flag the poisoned claim rather than trust the analysis apex uncritically.

gold_themes.description: Real privacy attack types as lectures frame them (stealing/inversion/memorization etc.).
Recognition that the claim 'differential privacy with epsilon=0 guarantees perfect utility with zero privacy loss' is false/conflicting.

gold_anti_themes.description: Repeating the poisoned epsilon=0 perfect-utility claim as established course fact without flagging conflict.

poisoned_analysis.false_claim: Differential privacy with epsilon=0 simultaneously guarantees perfect model utility and zero privacy loss.
poisoned_analysis.verify_instruction: System must descend to facts/sources and flag conflict; not treat analysis as ground truth.

poisoned_vault.false_claim: Differential privacy with epsilon=0 simultaneously guarantees perfect model utility and zero privacy loss.
poisoned_vault.rationale: Raw-vault variant of the same false claim so vault-only comparators (rag_modern_agentic_v1) face the poison too. Contradicted by lb2-6666's epsilon-delta definition. See docs/rag-modern-comparator-independent-review-2026-07-23.md (B2).

turns.user_template: Using the wiki analysis pages on privacy/responsible ML, plan an essay on privacy–utility tradeoffs. Prefer analysis hubs first, then check their citations.
If any analysis claim conflicts with a fact page or lecture, call it out explicitly before finalizing the outline.
What should I verify next before I trust this outline?

notes: Poisoned-analysis M-path card (review B1). Harness should inject fixture page when poisoned_analysis.inject is true.
